title.narrative: Promotion of human rights in the media

description.narrative: Contract related to: Promotion of human rights in the media - The Covid-19 pandemic is having significant negative repercussions on human rights, democracy and the rule of law in many parts of the world  and on the space for civil society organisations active in the promotion of human rights and democracy. An urgent reaction is required in the third quarter of 2021 to limit the harm done and contain further entrenchment and worsening of the situation.  The overall objective of the action is the worldwide promotion and protection of: (i) human rights and fundamental freedoms; (ii) democracy; and (iii) the rule of law. The action will achieve this so by supporting and strengthening civil society organisations (CSOs), democracy activists and human-rights defenders working on critical human rights and democracy in non-EU countries. It may also cover, where relevant, the promotion of international humanitarian law. The action will mainly be implemented through competitive processes.This action will mainly be implemented by EU delegations in-country so as to: (i) better respond to the country-specific contexts; (ii) take into account the local challenges of the current COVID-19 crisis; (iii) be as close as possible to the needs of the rights holders; and (iv) promote a sense of `ownership¿ of the action among local actors. The grants will aim at implementing the priorities listed in annex III Annex of the Regulation (EU) 2021/947 in line with Human Rights and Democracy country strategies. Implementing these priorities will also contribute to the EU action plan on human rights and democracy 2020-2024. The actions financed under the country allocations will be in line with: (i) the relevant EU action plan for human rights and democracy; (ii) EU guidelines on human rights; and (iii) the respective Human Rights and Democracy country strategies. All actions will follow a human rights based approach putting people at the centre of actions and also focus on promoting gender equality.

title.narrative: Conducting an aphorism contest

description.narrative: As part of World Press Freedom Day, celebrated on May 3, our centre launched a contest on social networks for the best aphorism about freedom of speech. The competition aimed to draw attention to the importance of freedom of speech.The contest participants were invited to write their version of the aphorism about freedom of speech and publish it on social networks using a specific hashtag or send it to us by email. Thus, we have ensured the participation of both active users of social networks and those who prefer a different way of participation.As the competitions main prize, participation in our training event was offered, allowing the winner to enrich their knowledge and skills in freedom of speech and media. The second and third places were rewarded with merchandising from our organization, which further motivated the contest participants.The total number of participants who participated in the competition was about 20. Participants were from Kazakhstan regions, indicating comprehensive coverage and interest in freedom of speech.The contest was successful, as it attracted the attention of a broad audience and stimulated participation in the discussion of essential topics related to freedom of speech. We have received a lot of exciting and original aphorisms that reflect the importance and relevance of this topic in modern society.Holding the contest honouring World Press Freedom Day was a positive and productive event. It helped draw attention to the importance of freedom of speech.

title.narrative: A study tour to Lithuania aiming to enhance cooperation between the lead applicant and coapplicant organisations

description.narrative: From May 17 to May 23, the Legal Media Center took part in a study trip to Lithuania. The primary purpose of this trip was to expand the potential of our organization and to exchange experience in the field of lobbying legislation effectively, judicial practice in cases against journalists in Lithuania, as well as to study the features of WEB2 and WEB3 technologies and the development of independent media in Europe.During the trip, our delegation held several meetings with highranking representatives of various organizations and institutions. We met with representatives of the Prosecutor Generals Office, the Ministry of Culture, and the Ombudsman of the Parliament, as well as with members of the Committee on Culture of the Parliament of the Republic of Lithuania. In addition, we visited the news portal Delfi. lt, where a meeting with his representative and the Inspector of Journalistic Ethics office occurred. We met with the Lithuanian branch of Transparency International.Together with our leading partner of the Lithuanian Union of Journalists project, we have been actively working on developing the structure of the journalistic ethics program, one of the projects results. This exchange of experience allowed us not only to learn new knowledge but also to share our expertise.

title.narrative: World Press Freedom Index country score according to the Reporters Without Borders (RSF)

description.narrative: The Index is compiled by pooling the responses of experts to a questionnaire devised by the RSF. This qualitative analysis is combined with quantitative data on abuses and acts of violence against journalists during the period evaluated. The criteria evaluated in the questionnaire are pluralism, media independence, media environment and selfcensorship, legislative framework, transparency, and the quality of the infrastructure that supports the production of news and information.Country scores range from 0 to 100 (with 0 being the best possible score and 100 the worst).

title.narrative: Information campaigns on social networks

description.narrative: Within the framework of the project, the topics of media law and the law on mass media were actively covered. The main goal of the information campaign was to increase the legal literacy of media representatives. The format and presentation of information flexibly changed depending on the agenda to achieve this goal.Weekly posts were published under the heading Question and Answer, where journalists questions were answered, and topical legal aspects related to the media were covered. The questions were selected from among the appeals to the legal service of Mediacoldau. This allowed for continuous feedback from the audience.In addition, a new media act from the world of journalism was presented every two weeks under the heading Media Act. This section aimed to attract the audiences attention and create interesting materials that helped to visualize and remember key moments in the media field.The total coverage of publications during the project was 7000 likes, which indicates a significant interest of the audience in this topic. Audience engagement was also high 5000, which shows the success of the presented content and its compliance with the needs of the target group.It should be noted that the information campaign has covered almost all regions of Kazakhstan, but the central part of the audience is concentrated in cities Astana, Kokshetau, Almaty. This indicates the importance of continuing work in these regions and the possibility of expanding coverage in other cities of the country.
